title: Guide - Healing and Hope - Small steps forward

parts.style: warm, gentle welcome, steady and unhurried
parts.text: Welcome to Healing and Hope. <short pause> This practice is called Small Steps Forward. <short pause> You won't be asked to feel better by the end of it. <short pause> We are only looking for the next small thing.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: Wherever you are, stop for a moment. <short pause> Let your shoulders come down by the width of a finger. <short pause> Let your jaw loosen. <short pause> Breathe out slowly... <short pause> and notice that for this one breath, you are not required to go anywhere.

There was a prophet named Elijah, who had been very brave for a very long time. <short pause> Then one day, his courage ran out. <short pause> He walked into the wilderness, sat down beneath a juniper tree, and told God that he had had enough. <short pause> And then, worn all the way through, he fell asleep.

He was not given a speech. <short pause> He was not scolded. <short pause> An angel touched him, and there by his head was bread, baked on the coals, and a jar of water. <short pause> He ate, and he drank, and he lay down again. <short pause> And God let him. <short pause> Then, in First Kings chapter nineteen, verse seven, we read this.
And the angel of the Lord came again the second time, and touched him, and said, Arise and eat; because the journey is too great for thee.

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: The journey is too great for thee. <short pause> What a kind thing to hear. <short pause> Not, you should be further along by now. <short pause> Not, others would manage this. <short pause> It is too much... so here is bread. <short pause> Heaven's plan for an exhausted man began with a meal, and sleep, and a gentle hand.

Healing often begins that way. <short pause> It is rarely a straight road. <short pause> There are days you walk, and days you lie down again under the tree. <short pause> A harder day doesn't erase the steps you have taken. <short pause> And rest is not the opposite of going forward. <short pause> Sometimes, it is the step.

So what is your bread and water today? <short pause> Something small enough to be done while you are still tired. <short pause> A glass of water. A shower. Opening the curtain. <short pause> Taking the medicine, or keeping the appointment. <short pause> Answering one message with, I'm having a hard day. <short pause> Let one of them come to mind... only one.

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: Now picture yourself doing it, slowly. <short pause> Where your hands will be. <short pause> What you will touch first. <short pause> If it still feels too great, make it smaller. <short pause> Not the shower... just the towel. <short pause> Not the walk... just the shoes. <short pause> When it is small enough, give it to God, and say... with You, this much.

This much is enough for today. <short pause> You don't have to see all forty days of the road. <short pause> Elijah couldn't, beneath his tree. <short pause> And you don't have to walk it unhelped. <short pause> A doctor, a counselor, a friend with a pot of soup... <short pause> any of them may be how the bread arrives.

Let's pray. <short pause> Father, You know when the journey is too great for me. <short pause> Feed me with what I need for this day. <short pause> Let me rest without shame, and rise without hurry. <short pause> Bless the one small step I can take... <short pause> and meet me again for the next. <short pause> Amen.
When you're ready, take your one small thing with you. <short pause> Do it gently, and let it count. <short pause> And when you have done it... <short pause> you may rest.
